text:
Mia: Quick post-mortem from the 90k-request perf run earlier today — attaching a short summary of kernel hotspots and a couple hypotheses.
Mia: Topline: runtime latency regressed ~12% on p99 for short prompts (<=64) after the batching heuristics change. Trace attached.
Mia: nsys snapshot: small-steps timeline shows repeated micro-bursts where attention kernels dominate. Not a single long kernel, many mid-duration launches that look like KV-related work.
Raj: can you paste the top kernel table?
Mia: pasted below (from nsys + flame sampling):
```
softmax_fused_attention.cu              28.4%
attention_kv_update.cu                 18.7%
kv_cache_lookup_local.cu               12.9%
fused_gemm_out.cu                       9.6%
layernorm_fwd.cu                        6.3%
recv/serialize_overhead                 5.2%
other small kernels                     18.9%
```
Mia: Note: softmax_fused includes both causal masking and rotary ops in our fused kernel, so that 28% is actually split across two codepaths depending on seq_len.
Kevin: interesting — where is SM util and occupancy during the bursts?
Mia: snapshot: sm_util spiking to 95% but occupancy falling ~40% vs baseline. Looks like fewer warps but heavier per-warp work (tensor ops). Perfetto timeline shows repeated kernel handoffs with short gaps of memcpy for KV.
Eva: KV cache thrash hypothesis — the new batching groups slightly different session sequences so the prefix cache hit rate drops. Do we have KV hit metrics?
Mia: yes. KV hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 63% for short prompts under the new batching window. That's the smoking gun in my mind.
Sam: That would increase attention_kv_update and kv_cache_lookup costs; those line up. Any correlation with batch size changes?
Mia: We increased dynamic_batch_timeout_ms from 8 -> 28 to reduce RPC calls; average batch size rose 1.6x but the batch composition changed (more mixed seq_len sessions).
Raj: So bigger batches but less prefix coalescing. Makes sense. Could push more interleaving of unrelated sessions into the same batch causing KV misses.
Kevin: For a quick experiment, can we try two things: (1) re-enable per-session batch affinity (cheap flag), (2) revert timeout to 10ms. If latency recovers, we proved batching-affinity regress.
Mia: I ran a quick A/B on a small pool: reverting timeout -> p99 latency recovered ~7% and KV hit-rate back to 82%. Per-session affinity flag gave a further ~3% improvement.
perf-bot: nsys report uploaded: https://perf-artifacts/redwood/2365456789/nsys-summary.html
Eva: Nice. What's the plan for kernel-side mitigations? We shouldn't trade cost for correctness forever.
Mia: Two parallel paths:
- short: change batching heuristic to prefer prefix-homogeneous grouping (weight = 1.4) and add a small KV-prefetch micro-op in the runtime when batch contains mixed sessions.
- medium: tune kernel launch to pre-warm KV lanes: add tiny kernel that warms L2/KV structures before the attention kernels in mixed batches. Prototype shows ~6% reduction in attention_kv_update tail.
Raj: Do we risk increasing GPU occupancy pressure with pre-warm kernel? Might add latency for all requests.
Mia: pre-warm kernel is extremely lightweight (single CTA, launches async) — but yes need to validate under heavy throughput.
Kevin: Another idea: adjust kernel selection — use a variant of fused_attention that is slightly more warp-friendly (less register pressure) for short-seq mixed batches. We have a quantized kernel variant that trades some FLOPs for lower regs.
Sam: Was there a regression in register spilling reported by nvprof?
Mia: nvprof shows occasional L1 traffic upticks and a slight increase in local memory usage on the softmax_fused kernel for mixed batches. That's consistent with different code path (rotary vs no-rotary toggles).
Eva: Action items?
Mia: short: revert timeout to 10ms on canary hosts + enable per-session batch affinity flag (rolled out to 10% now). Monitor p50/p95/p99 + KV hit-rate.
Mia: medium: bench pre-warm kernel and low-reg fused_attention variant — target: reduce attention_kv_update by 25% tail.
Mia: long: update runtime batching optimizer to include KV-hit probability model; tune grouping weight automatically.
Raj: I'll own the canary revert rollout and dashboards.
Kevin: I'll prototype low-reg fused kernel and run microbenchmarks.
Eva: I'll instrument KV-hit telemetry and produce a daily trend.
Sam: I'll add an automated perf test in CI that runs a synthetic mixed-batch workload and checks KV-hit and p99 regression thresholds.
Mia: Thanks all. If anyone wants the raw perfetto/trace files ping me and I'll share.
perf-bot: perf check: p99 increased by 12% on experiment cluster; rollback/flags recommended.
Mia: attaching perfetto snippet for the burst region (timeline snippet id: perfetto://trace/2365456789/burst-clip)
Mia: TL;DR: regression comes from batching heuristic -> KV hit drop -> increased attention_kv_update + softmax_fused pressure. Immediate mitigation: revert timeout + batch affinity. Medium-term: kernel variants and pre-warm optimization.
Kevin: 👍 I'll post preliminary kernel bench results by EOD tomorrow.
Raj: rolling change now. Monitoring channel: #eng-runtime-perf (I tagged the dashboard).
